items.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009
items.q: There was bass players like Oscar Pettiford and Ray Brown and Percy Heath and bass players like that... you know if you wanted to get wise about anything about playing, sometime you’ll want to say something or play something by one of these musicians like Percy Heath or Ray Brown.

ctx.x: For the bass player, for all of jazz history to that point, you were supposed to be the provider of the harmony, the root, and keep things, keep the form going that way. Did that start to change for the bass? That you could be freer.

It caused more playing than I was doing. It caused more playing to be played by that means. There was bass players like Oscar Pettiford and Ray Brown and Percy Heath and bass players like that, Israel Crosby and two more, you know, very good bass players, technically. I mean you know if you wanted to get wise about anything about playing, sometime you’ll want to say something or play something by one of these musicians like Percy Heath or Ray Brown.
So most of your people that you listened to, you saw them in New York, you’re — it’s sort of people that you wanted to emulate or heard on records? Is that right?
